source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Power on and boot in BIOS.
2. Press load default,save and reboot.
3. Boot in BIOS,compare setting should matches SPEC.
4. Change BIOS all/random setting in this function,to non-default  setting.
5. Save and reboot.
6. Boot in BIOS and check your setting still exist.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. The default setting should matches SPEC."
2. No error log happen.
3. Normal reboot ,no hang、crash happen.
4. Check your set still exist.

original_test_intent: Verify Boot settings defaults and persistence of approved non-default controls without selecting an unintended device or remote image, bypassing the approved Secure Boot/CSM policy, losing local recovery or preventing the intended OS from booting.
original_method: Manually load defaults, compare named boot fields and ordered persistent targets with SPEC, apply a bounded target/policy matrix, save and use the documented reset, verify persistence and the exact approved boot result, then restore the final order.
manual_activity: An engineer must operate and visually accept firmware boot controls and observe the actual selected boot path. Automated boot-entry and OS evidence is supporting only.
required_inputs: Persistent identities for local storage, removable media and network boot entries
SPEC defaults, approved order/timeout/policy values and expected fallback behavior
Secure Boot/CSM state plus approved image/service digests and identities
Known-good signed local recovery and independent console/OOB
safety_requirements: Never operationalize all/random or point firmware to an unapproved device, PXE/HTTP service or image.
Identify boot entries by persistent device and image identity, not display order or volatile Boot#### number alone.
Do not weaken Secure Boot/CSM policy as a shortcut and do not permit unattended deployment to production storage.
Protect a signed local recovery target and independent console/OOB path.
Stop on wrong target/image, unexpected network contact, trust-policy change, boot failure or management loss.
Restore the approved final order/state; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Collect read-only UEFI boot variables/entries where safely exposed, persistent storage/NIC identities, image digests, Secure Boot state, boot logs, selected-root identity and BMC health.
Correlate each reboot with the actual approved target without modifying entries or services.
Do not drive BIOS, change boot variables, start deployment, boot unapproved media or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve fields, target/order matrix, trust dependencies, fallback, reset and recovery.
Perform and capture default-first and bounded non-default firmware phases and observe target selection.
Interpret boot/trust/device evidence and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly rejects agent BIOS execution. No source command exists; efibootmgr or OS bootloader edits would change another control path and are not equivalent substitutions.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Preserve the firmware method and add version-recorded read-only UEFI entry, persistent target, image, trust and boot-result evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The default-first lifecycle, null script and 5/20-minute fields are retained; all/random remains source text only.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Map each firmware control and boot entry to immutable device/service/image identity, define expected selection/fallback for each bounded state, and correlate firmware captures with the actually booted root or network transaction.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact UEFI boot manager, devices, network services, Secure Boot/CSM state and project images.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS/BMC, device/NIC firmware, bootloader/OS and evidence-tool versions plus image digests.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform boot-manager documentation and approved Secure Boot/network-boot policy.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces random changes with identity-based target/order/fallback scenarios and explicit trust/recovery controls.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; preserves defaults/persistence and adds actual target, image provenance and fallback coverage.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Fields, persistent targets, orders, images/services, trust and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: UEFI entry numbering can change and firmware UI labels may be ambiguous; persistent hardware/image identity is mandatory.

project_override_considerations: A project may select named local, removable or network targets and approved order scenarios. Results must list excluded target classes and cannot claim all boot paths.
expected_evidence: Platform identity, field/default/target matrix, image/service approvals and recovery
Baseline persistent target IDs, boot entries/order, trust state and health
Load Default captures plus SPEC and actual default-target comparison
Non-default captures, persistence and identity-correlated boot/fallback result
Approved final order/state, logs and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The default-first and persistence lifecycle agrees with the criteria. Exact targets and policies are project readiness inputs, not contradictory facts.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The boot-setting lifecycle is clear. Missing target/image/recovery inputs prevents a run but does not permanently block the master case.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agrees on manual firmware operation and adds persistent target, trust and recovery safeguards.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its entry/Secure Boot/device evidence while correcting classification to MANUAL ONLY.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates firmware acceptance from read-only boot evidence and rejects OS variable editing as a substitute.

review_improvement: Prevents a persisted boot order from being accepted when firmware selected the wrong physical device, remote service or image, or removed signed local recovery.
independent_technical_reasoning: The core operation and acceptance are firmware UI actions plus observation of the selected path. Automation can corroborate identity but cannot complete those manual steps, so MANUAL ONLY is required.
no_automatic_retry: Do not automatically repeat boot-setting changes, target selections, boots or recovery after wrong-target, trust, boot or management anomalies; preserve first evidence and obtain engineer disposition.
